area_note: This is a small core. Architectural state is the 1024-bit register file, plus reg_pc/next_pc/op1/op2/out (160 bits), plus 2x64 counters, plus decoder and FSM state: about 1.5k flops outside the register file and about 2.5k bits in total. fast_mul adds a 33x33 multiplier with 64-bit result registers, and div adds about 190 flops. A 16-word operand buffer (512 bits) is half the register file and about 20% of the core's state, which is a large cost. The existing red_accel (2x16 words = 1024 bits, plus a second 32x32 multiplier) roughly doubles the core's flop count.
constraints: PCPI itself cannot reach memory. A memory-operand instruction works only through red_core's acc_busy bus mux: the unit must assert busy and pcpi_wait for the whole time it owns the bus, and must drive mem_valid only while busy.
The CPU is fully stalled while the accelerator runs. There is no overlap between accelerator work and CPU execution.
One bus beat costs 2 cycles and only one transaction is outstanding, so a unit that streams N words pays at least 2N cycles.
Only 2 source registers and one 32-bit rd result are available per instruction.
The unit must assert pcpi_wait or pcpi_ready within about 16 cycles of pcpi_valid, or the core traps (pcpi_timeout, CATCH_ILLINSN=1).
pcpi_ready must be a single-cycle pulse, and the unit must not accept a new instruction until pcpi_valid drops. red_accel uses an S_WAIT state for this.
Custom-0 funct3=000/funct7=0 is already taken by red_accel. Choose another funct3/funct7 or custom-1/2/3.
The core already has a 32x32 multiplier. A second multiplier inside the accelerator costs area twice, and red_accel already pays it.
There are no interrupts and no compressed instructions, so firmware must be RV32IM only.
The baseline and the extended core differ only in ENABLE_PCPI and red_accel. Every cycle or area difference counts against the extension.
coprocessor: PCPI (Pico Co-Processor Interface). Any instruction the core does not decode (instr_trap) is offered to PCPI. In ld_rs1, which is dual-port, the core drives pcpi_valid=1 with pcpi_insn, pcpi_rs1 (reg_op1) and pcpi_rs2 (reg_op2). The unit must answer within about 16 cycles with pcpi_wait or pcpi_ready, or pcpi_timeout traps it as an illegal instruction. It then raises pcpi_ready with pcpi_wr/pcpi_rd and the core goes back to fetch. PCPI itself carries no address or data bus: it only receives 2 register values and returns 1. Memory access comes from RED's wrapper, not from PCPI: red_core.v has a 1-bit bus mux on acc_busy. While red_accel holds busy, which it does while stalling the CPU through pcpi_wait, it drives mem_valid, mem_addr, mem_wdata and mem_wstrb itself, and the CPU's mem_ready is forced to 0. That makes the accelerator a bus master with an arbiter that already exists. The shipped red_accel.v uses this to load 16 words, multiply, and store 16 words.
coprocessor_result: At most one 32-bit value per instruction. pcpi_rd is written to rd only if pcpi_wr=1, and it arrives in the cycle pcpi_ready=1. Anything wider has to go to memory through the red_core bus mux, or take several instructions.
custom_opcode_space: custom-0 0001011: red_accel currently decodes funct3=000/funct7=0000000. Other funct3/funct7 values are free because ENABLE_IRQ=0, so picorv32's IRQ custom instructions are not decoded.
Do not use opcode 0110011 with funct7=0000001: fast_mul and div already decode it on the same PCPI bus.

existing_units: Single-cycle 32x32->64 signed array multiplier, picorv32_pcpi_fast_mul ($signed 33x33 *). It handles MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU with about 2 cycles of PCPI latency and pcpi_wait=0. The PCPI result mux gives external PCPI priority over it.
Sequential restoring divider, picorv32_pcpi_div: DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU at 1 bit per cycle, about 32+ cycles.
No barrel shifter (BARREL_SHIFTER=0). Shifts are iterative: 4 bits per cycle, then 1 bit per cycle (TWO_STAGE_SHIFT=1).
One 32-bit ALU for add/sub/compare/logic, single cycle (TWO_CYCLE_ALU=0, TWO_CYCLE_COMPARE=0).
The current red_accel.v already holds 32x32 words of operand/product buffers and its own 32x32 multiplier, which duplicates fast_mul.
isa: RV32IM with rdcycle/rdinstr counters. There is no C extension, no interrupts and no other CSRs. red_core sets ENABLE_MUL=0, ENABLE_FAST_MUL=1, ENABLE_DIV=1, COMPRESSED_ISA=0, ENABLE_IRQ=0, ENABLE_COUNTERS=1, and ENABLE_PCPI=ENABLE_ACCEL (1 for the extended core, 0 for the baseline).
memory_interface: PicoRV32 native valid/ready bus: mem_valid, mem_instr, mem_ready, 32-bit mem_addr/mem_wdata/mem_rdata, and 4-bit mem_wstrb. There is no burst mode and only one transaction is outstanding. The testbench (red_soc_tb.v) is a single-port RAM that returns ready one cycle after valid, so 2 cycles per word. MMIO: 0x10000000 putc, 0x10000004 exit, 0x10000008 cycle counter. The accelerator shares mem_rdata and receives mem_ready gated by acc_busy.
microarchitecture: Multi-cycle and not pipelined. A single FSM runs fetch -> ld_rs1 -> (ld_rs2) -> exec/shift/ldmem/stmem -> fetch. The next fetch overlaps only with exec (mem_do_prefetch). The core issues one memory transaction at a time on one shared bus. The testbench memory raises mem_ready one cycle after it sees mem_valid, so every bus beat takes 2 cycles. Estimates: ALU op about 4 cycles, load or store about 7, taken branch about 6, shift 4-14 cycles because TWO_STAGE_SHIFT steps 4 bits then 1 bit per cycle. Software here is slow, so a custom instruction competes against roughly 4-7 cycles per base instruction.
name: PicoRV32 inside RED's red_core (eval/rtl/red_core.v)
register_file: 32 x 32-bit registers (cpuregs, ENABLE_REGS_16_31=1). ENABLE_REGS_DUALPORT defaults to 1, so there are 2 read ports and both rs1 and rs2 values reach PCPI in the same cycle. There is 1 write port. The maximum is 2 register operands in and 1 register result out per instruction. rs3 is not supported.
